body.statement: For every fixed nondegenerate bounded class \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) containing the lower family, there exist \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\le\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), with \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) the symmetric aligned discrepancy. The primary class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}\) is justified directly by its \(C^2\) Hessian condition and has exponent \(3/4\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), the finite-type conditions imply direct componentwise circular recovery up to a common node permutation; this has the same conclusion type as the cited exact-identification results. The strengthened smoothness, conditioning, separation, and attained-order assumptions are used only for the uniform nonzero-error frontier.
body.justification: The theorem names the critical-order recovery frontier in a symmetric quotient geometry and separates the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse headline from the novel general finite-type rate class.
body.gap: Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. prove qualitative exact recovery under almost-everywhere discrepancy; no cited Morse theorem supplies the \(k=2\) rate assumptions, and no comparator gives a symmetric law-based sharp exponent at isolated critical points.
body.consumer: Likelihood and score-based causal representation learners obtain a calibrated translation from population objective error to encoder error.

obligation.what_is_open: The class-uniform upper inequality for arbitrary transition diffeomorphisms, including the primary two-node Morse case.
obligation.obstruction: Its only missing load-bearing premise is the unresolved full incompressible-rigidity estimate; substituting the proved radial subclass would change the quantified class.
obligation.attempted: The exact full-law residual reduction and the sharp radial interpolation were proved, and the principal packet counterexample families were checked without producing a legal full-law violation.
obligation.partial_result: The lower inequality is proved by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:localized\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\). The upper inequality would follow immediately by composing Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:full\text{-}law\text{-}residual\text{-}reduction}\) with an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\), but that resolution is not available. Thus the full two-sided statement, including the primary full-class \(3/4\) upper bound, remains open rather than being inferred from the radial theorem.
